title: WM-MT143-ConflictBridgeToMergeUi
clause: Bridge git conflict stages (:1:/:2:/:3:) into DiffEditorPanel Merge mode; write-back via git add; commit or clean abort

scope.summary:
GOAL: Bridge MergeOutcome::Conflicts (MT-142) into the EXISTING native 3-pane merge UI so a conflicted merge is resolved through DiffEditorPanel Merge mode and written back to the git index — no auto-resolution, no half-committed exits. The UI already exists and is reused, not rebuilt: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs has DiffMode { SideBySide, Inline, Merge } (~lines 73-81), DiffEditorPanel::merge constructing 3 panes local/base/remote with per-conflict Accept Local / Accept Remote / Accept Both, and MergeState { base, local, remote, blocks, merged } (~lines 244-252); diff_engine.rs (same crate) supplies the Myers diff. This MT supplies the missing data path in and the resolution path out.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) Backend: conflict-version extraction + resolution write-back functions added to src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs (module from MT-142). (b) Frontend: a NEW thin bridge module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/merge_conflict_bridge.rs that maps ConflictFileVersions -> DiffEditorPanel::merge inputs and maps the resolved merged buffer -> the backend write-back call; diff_editor_panel.rs itself is touched only if a minimal accessor for the merged output buffer is missing. (c) Tests both sides.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Backend types + signatures (source_control_merge.rs):
   pub struct ConflictFileVersions { pub path: String, pub base: Option<String>, pub local: Option<String>, pub remote: Option<String>, pub extension: String }
   impl MergeSession {
     pub fn conflict_file_versions(&self, conflict: &MergeConflict) -> Result<ConflictFileVersions, SourceControlError>
       // stage contents from the controlled checkout: `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true show :1:<path>` (base), `show :2:<path>` (local/ours = target), `show :3:<path>` (remote/theirs = source branch); a missing stage (add/add, delete/modify) => None and the UI pane renders empty-with-reason
     pub fn resolve_conflict(&self, path: &str, merged_contents: &str) -> Result<(), SourceControlError>
       // writes merged_contents to <checkout>/<path> then `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true add -- <literal_pathspec(path)>`
     pub fn unresolved_paths(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>, SourceControlError>   // `ls-files -u -z`, distinct paths still conflicted
     pub fn complete(&self, message: &str) -> Result<MergeOutcome, SourceControlError>
       // ONLY when unresolved_paths() is empty: `git -C <checkout> -c core.longpaths=true commit --no-gpg-sign -m <attributed message>` -> MergeOutcome::CleanMerged{fast_forward:false}; otherwise typed error MergeIncomplete { remaining: Vec<String> }
   }
2. Attribution: the completion commit message carries the merge attribution block: source branch, target branch, resolution session id, and per-file resolution origin (ui_operator | governed_session) as trailer lines (e.g. Merged-By-Session:, Resolved-Files:). The resolution session is recorded so audit (MT-145) can bind who resolved what.
3. Frontend bridge (merge_conflict_bridge.rs):
   pub struct MergeUiRequest { pub conflict: ConflictFileVersions }
   pub fn open_merge_panel(req: &MergeUiRequest) -> DiffEditorPanel   // DiffEditorPanel::merge(base, local, remote, &req.conflict.extension); empty string for a None stage plus a visible pane label ('(no base: add/add conflict)')
   pub fn take_resolution(panel: &DiffEditorPanel) -> Option<String> // the MergeState.merged output buffer once every MergeBlock has a chosen side; None while any block is unchosen
   The bridge NEVER chooses a side itself: chosen state comes only from the panel's Accept Local/Accept Remote/Accept Both interactions (operator or governed resolution session driving the same API).
4. Unresolved exit: if the resolution flow ends (panel closed, session ends, error) with unresolved_paths() non-empty and complete() not called, the caller MUST call MergeSession::abort(); MergeSession Drop (MT-142) guarantees it. The merge is left fully aborted — NEVER half-committed, no MERGE_HEAD, no partial index.
5. HARD RULES: no auto-resolution anywhere (bridge and backend refuse to fabricate a merged buffer); no force flags; no push; CRDT boundary — this bridge handles git CODE conflicts only, never kernel/crdt document state.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read diff_editor_panel.rs (DiffMode ~73-81, MergeState ~244-252, DiffEditorPanel::merge constructor, accept-button block handling) and diff_engine.rs public functions.
2. Implement conflict_file_versions with `git show :N:<path>`, mapping missing stages to None; extension derived from the path (fallback 'txt').
3. Implement resolve_conflict (write file + `git add --`), unresolved_paths, complete with MergeIncomplete guard and attribution trailers.
4. Implement merge_conflict_bridge.rs mapping versions -> DiffEditorPanel::merge and merged-output extraction; add a minimal merged-buffer accessor to diff_editor_panel.rs only if none exists.
5. Backend tests: conflicted scratch repo -> versions match `git rev-parse` stage oids; resolve_conflict clears the path from ls-files -u; complete() refuses while conflicts remain (MergeIncomplete), commits when clear; abort-on-unresolved leaves pristine state.
6. Frontend tests (egui_kittest/AccessKit headless, same style as existing diff panel tests): 3 panes populated from a ConflictFileVersions fixture; choosing Accept Local/Remote/Both per block yields the expected merged buffer; take_resolution None while a block is unchosen.
7. End-to-end test (backend-driven, headless): real conflicted merge -> versions -> programmatic accept choices through the SAME bridge API -> resolve_conflict -> complete -> merge commit exists with attribution trailers; and the negative twin: close-without-resolve -> aborted, no MERGE_HEAD.
8. Run proof targets.
allowed_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs (minimal merged-output accessor only; no pane/interaction redesign)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (GUI IPC allowed only on the GUI MT, MT-146)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/** (CRDT document merging is a separate domain; do not conflate with git worktree code merge)
acceptance_criteria: conflict_file_versions returns base/local/remote contents matching `git show :1:/:2:/:3:` for a real conflicted path, with None for missing stages (add/add case proven).
resolve_conflict writes the merged buffer and stages it via `git add --` with literal pathspec; the path disappears from `ls-files -u`.
complete() commits ONLY when zero unresolved paths remain, with --no-gpg-sign and attribution trailers naming source, target, and resolution session; MergeIncomplete typed error otherwise.
Unresolved exit is provably safe: ending the flow without complete() leaves the merge aborted — no MERGE_HEAD, pristine target checkout, target ref unchanged (never half-committed).

merge_conflict_bridge feeds DiffEditorPanel::merge (existing DiffMode::Merge, MergeState) without duplicating any diff/merge UI logic; take_resolution returns None until every MergeBlock has a chosen side.
No auto-resolution: neither backend nor bridge fabricates or defaults a chosen side; end-to-end test drives choices exclusively through the bridge API the UI uses.
Zero occurrences of '--force', 'push', '-X', '--ours', '--theirs' in source_control_merge.rs and merge_conflict_bridge.rs.
All new git invocations include -c core.longpaths=true.
A resolution-session record (session id + resolved paths) is produced for audit consumption (typed struct returned from complete(), persisted by MT-145 wiring).
code_surfaces: src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs (extends MT-142 MergeSession: conflict_file_versions, resolve_conflict, unresolved_paths, complete)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs (REUSE: DiffMode::Merge ~73-81, DiffEditorPanel::merge, MergeState ~244-252, Accept Local/Accept Remote/Accept Both)
expected_tests: backend: stage extraction equals git rev-parse :1/:2/:3 blob contents; add/add yields base=None
backend: resolve+complete produces a merge commit whose tree contains the resolved contents; trailers present
backend: complete() with remaining conflicts => MergeIncomplete{remaining} and no commit
backend: drop-without-complete => aborted, no MERGE_HEAD, ref unchanged
frontend (headless egui_kittest/AccessKit): 3 panes populated; per-block Accept choices produce expected merged buffer; unchosen block => take_resolution None
end-to-end: real conflict resolved programmatically through the bridge API -> committed merge; twin negative: closed unresolved -> aborted
implementation_notes: Stage semantics in a merge run from the TARGET checkout: :2: (ours) = target/local pane, :3: (theirs) = source-branch/remote pane, :1: = common base pane — label panes exactly this way so the UI's local/base/remote wording matches git reality.

Binary conflicts: `git show :N:` returns bytes; if content is not valid UTF-8, return a typed NotTextResolvable error — binary conflict resolution is out of scope and must surface as a blocked conflict, never a mangled lossy-UTF8 auto-write.
Path safety: reuse literal_pathspec/normalize_repo_path from source_control.rs so paths with spaces/globs cannot escape the pathspec.

The governed-resolution-session path drives the SAME bridge API as the operator UI (programmatic Accept choices); MT-148 proves this equivalence live — keep the API side-effect-free until resolve_conflict.
Merge-review annotations on resolved files are an OPTIONAL later layer (MT-201+ annotations family); do not build annotation storage here.
MT-146 mounts this bridge in the operator flow; keep merge_conflict_bridge free of pane-registry/shell wiring so MT-146 can mount it as a pane without rework.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Data/logic bridge into the EXISTING DiffEditorPanel Merge mode; no new operator surface is mounted here. The operator-facing merge-review flow with Argus evidence is MT-146. Frontend proof here is headless egui_kittest/AccessKit.

target_entries: Source Control > Resolving merge conflicts (3-pane local/base/remote, Accept Local/Remote/Both, write-back, completion commit)
Source Control > Conflict safety (unresolved exit always aborts; binary conflicts surface as blocked; no auto-resolution)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Conflicted/resolved/aborted FR kinds are MT-161 seam wired by MT-145; this MT returns the typed resolution-session record MT-145 persists.
Diagnostic event on stage-extraction failure or non-UTF8 conflict surfacing, if the open diagnostic-event API exists in the implementing worktree.
No long-lived process introduced; UI liveness is covered by the app-level watchers, not per-bridge.

risk_if_missed: Conflicted merges dead-end: MT-142 can detect conflicts but nobody can resolve them inside Handshake, so operators drop to raw git (unaudited, error-prone) and MT-146/148 cannot ship.

risks: RISK-1: Pane mislabeling (ours/theirs swapped) makes the operator confidently accept the WRONG side — a silent data-destroying resolution that all tests pass if they share the same swap.
RISK-2: complete() commits while unresolved paths remain (or a partial `git add` marks a conflict resolved with markers still in the file), producing a merge commit containing '<<<<<<<' garbage.
RISK-3: A default/fallback chosen side in the bridge quietly auto-resolves blocks the operator never looked at, violating the no-auto-resolution hard rule.
RISK-4: Unresolved exit leaks MERGE_HEAD/staged state (half-committed), permanently blocking later merges with MergeAlreadyInProgress.
RISK-5: Non-UTF8/binary conflict content is lossily converted and written back, corrupting binary assets.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Stage-mapping test asserts against independently-computed git rev-parse blob contents with DIFFERENT distinctive markers per side (base/local/remote sentinel strings), so a swap cannot cancel out; pane labels come from one shared const mapping.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): complete() re-runs ls-files -u at commit time (not cached state) and additionally greps the staged resolved files for conflict-marker lines ('<<<<<<<'/'>>>>>>>') as a tripwire, refusing with a typed error.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): take_resolution returns None unless EVERY MergeBlock has an explicit chosen side; test asserts an untouched panel never yields a resolution.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Drop/abort guarantee inherited from MT-142 is re-proven at this layer: kill-mid-resolution test asserts no MERGE_HEAD, empty status, unchanged target ref.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Non-UTF8 stage content => typed NotTextResolvable, no write-back path exists for it; test uses a real binary blob conflict.

research_provenance.source: Verified current code: wtc-native-editors-v1 src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs — DiffMode { SideBySide, Inline, Merge } lines 73-81, Merge = 3 panes local/base/remote with per-conflict accept buttons, MergeState { base, local, remote, blocks, merged } lines 244-252, DiffEditorPanel::merge constructor; diff_engine.rs Myers diff in the same crate. wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 source_control.rs literal_pathspec/normalize_repo_path + commit --no-gpg-sign ~275. Field practice: git mergetool's :1:/:2:/:3: stage-extraction + `git add` write-back is the canonical external-mergetool contract (git-scm mergetool docs); this bridge reimplements that contract against the in-app panel instead of an external tool.
corrections: Reuse decision: the existing DiffEditorPanel Merge mode is the UI — this MT is data-in/resolution-out only; building a second merge view was rejected.
Hard rules baked in: no auto-resolution (explicit per-block choices only), unresolved exit aborts (never half-committed), no force/push, git code-merge vs CRDT document-merge boundary stated.
Merge-review annotations deferred to the MT-201+ annotations family (optional mention only, per family seam map).
